title: Photonic chips adopted faster than expected: Discover -> plans

expected.behavior: Return 1-3 candidates, each with one of the three evidence labels; Inspect the first grounded candidate. Within that direction, branch only where there is a real dispute (one branch is fine if there is none); one plan per terminal. At least one numeric condition, with a threshold grounded in the pack or null plus threshold_note. Address the counter-evidence in the pack (sc-036 ramp timing, sc-025 laser count, sc-043 integrated-laser route): either mark the claim contradicted or explain why it is not a rebuttal.

human_review: E1: does the cited text support each edge's mechanism
E1: is the counter-evidence addressed
E2: if this numeric condition were removed, would the thesis still stand
Branch quality: are the branches real competitors, not padding

title: Models stronger than Fable get export-restricted -> user-given target: Inspect

expected.behavior: Give an A -> B causal path (branching and merging allowed) or no_chain with a reason. At least one document or event condition (the formal export-control filing, effective date, licence requirement); anchor and deadline are absolute dates or a user-specified scenario start. No invented numeric thresholds. Every plan's gate is WAIT.

human_review: E1: is every hop of the path grounded in the pack
E2: are the document / event conditions specific, decidable and logically tied to the thesis

title: Fork the C1 baseline graph: ChangeAssumption + AddShock

expected.behavior: The model marks exactly the golden claims as challenged. Write scope, out-of-scope hashes, new-edge identification and baseline retention are code behavior covered by the functional tests; here only the model's assessment is judged.

actual.summary: change_assumption: challenged=['c1.laser_demand', 'c1.term.laser_vendor'], out-of-scope writes=1 | add_shock: challenged=['c1.siph_foundry', 'c1.term.foundry'], out-of-scope writes=1

human_review: E3: does the diff text present the scenario as an observation (it may only say 'challenged', never 'invalidated')

title: Midterm split -> distant target: Discover should abstain

expected.behavior: Discover abstains explicitly (0 candidates), or returns only not_recommended candidates with an explanation; proposals is an empty list; no target is forced into a plan.

human_review: E4: is the abstention reason substantive (not a platitude)
E4: did the model use sc-039 / sc-040 (LITE excerpts) to force an election -> LITE chain

title: Strait of Hormuz reopens next week: no invented numbers across domains

expected.behavior: Run the full flow. The transit condition's threshold stays null with a threshold_note, but the real pack now has a pre-closure baseline (hz-009): the note should cite it and say the user must confirm what level counts as recovery, not claim there is no baseline. 'Next week' is clarified into a dated judgment the user must confirm. Reopening has not happened yet, so it should be role=shock and the related branch hypothetical. Address the counter-evidence (after the June reopening transits stayed under half; the strait closed again). Every plan's gate is WAIT.

human_review: E1: is the counter-evidence addressed
E2: are entry / exit conditions specific and decidable
E2: does threshold_note cite the pre-closure baseline hz-009 instead of inventing a number or saying there is no baseline
Branch quality: is the not-yet-happened reopening marked role=shock
